answer: Each identity registers one anchor bearing a relic serial plate, locks a 75-credit bond, and files one gale-load log with gust speed and anchor tension. An auditor recomputes expected tension from the public anchor-load table; missing, copied, or reused logs burn the bond. The first filing costs 30 credits, the kth costs 30+9(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 9,021 and 1,000 fake identities pay 4,525,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-anchor ring fails because each log binds one serial plate to one identity key, so duplicate serials expose it on the register. An honest agent pays 30 once.
